title: #164 initial-condition screen, variant D -- the same pre-#164 bench (EN DC-high) started cold with `uic`
claim: Variant D of the four-variant initial-condition screen behind issue #164: variant A's testbench file, byte-for-byte (deliberately shared rather than copied, so the two records' netlist snapshots are identical and the ONLY difference between them is the analysis card), run with `tran 10u 3m uic` -- every node starts at 0 with EN already DC-high. What it is evidence FOR/AGAINST: it answers "is the rail mode a start-up failure?" and it isolates which half of the shipped fix is load-bearing. If all 200 draws arrive at regulation from a cold start, the loop always starts, so no start-up assist is warranted; and if D matches variant C (the shipped bench, which adds an EN edge on top of `uic`), then `uic` alone is what closes the finding and the EN edge is house-convention alignment with sim/startup rather than the fix. SUBSTANTIATES NO SPEC ROW. This is diagnostic evidence for design/README.md's "#164" section (the four-variant initial-condition screen), deliberately kept in its own experiment slug so that measurements/build_characterization_report.py -- which reads the LEXICOGRAPHICALLY LAST record under sim/<slug>/records/ for the slug a spec row maps to -- cannot ever pick a screen variant up as the Output row's evidence. EVIDENCE_MAP maps "Output" to sim/mc-output-accuracy and nothing maps to this slug, the same way sim/pdk-smoke is harness-only rather than a spec claim. The shipped, spec-substantiating Output-row bench and record are sim/mc-output-accuracy and 20260925-131502-808cece (variant C of this same screen); nothing here supersedes, re-grades or replaces them. The vout_ss card keeps the ratified +-2% window verbatim anyway, so this variant's pass/fail tally is directly comparable with sim/mc-output-accuracy's records -- comparability is the point of the screen.

mc_corner.note: The same single mismatch-enabled point sim/mc-output-accuracy characterizes (tt_mm, 27 C, VIN 3.3 V, 1 mA) -- held fixed across all four screen variants on purpose: the screen varies the INITIAL CONDITION and nothing else.

mc_analysis.note: SCREEN VARIANT D -- `uic` added to variant A's otherwise-identical deck, with EN left as a DC level (no edge). Deliberately NOT the shipped bench: the shipped bench (variant C, sim/mc-output-accuracy) carries both `uic` AND the 100 us EN edge, and separating them is this variant's entire job.

mc_measurements.name: vout_ss
mc_measurements.spice: .meas tran vout_ss avg v(vout) from=2.5m to=3m
mc_measurements.note: Steady-state VOUT averaged over the settled tail (2.5ms-3ms of a 3ms transient), identical card and identical ratified window (spec/target-spec.md "Output", 1.8V +-2%, ratified by issue #1 / DR-006) to the one sim/mc-output-accuracy uses -- kept identical so this screen variant's tally is comparable with that bench's records. This slug substantiates no spec row; see the experiment claim.

mc_measurements.name: fb_ss
mc_measurements.spice: .meas tran fb_ss avg v(xldo.fb) from=2.5m to=3m
mc_measurements.note: Node dump (unbounded -- diagnostic, no limit and therefore no verdict): settled V(xldo.fb), averaged over the same tail as vout_ss. Why this node: the divider tap the error amp compares against VREF -- the node whose 668-1984 V (and 1.3e15 V) settled values are the whole finding: FB is fed ONLY by VOUT through a passive three-leg res_xhigh_po string, so any realizable state has 0 <= V(N_FBB) <= V(FB) <= V(VOUT) <= VIN.
